admission.justification: The publication, the observer model, the projection reader and the builder must agree per prompt, not per agent: a sibling's resolution would otherwise take an unanswered prompt off the queue, and a fabricated identity would make a second prompt look like the first. The sibling-resolution and retention cases pin both failures.

applicability: Permission identities admitted from at most 32 sorted published prompt IDs per agent and at most 128 permission rows across the served population.
conditions: The host serializes at most 32 sorted outstanding IDs per agent; exceeding that cap makes its publication incomplete. The input reader separately admits the first 128 rows ordered by agent ID and prompt order. Aggregate overflow can omit or displace a row without resolving it.

A row that remains admitted keeps its actual agent and prompt identity through publication, projection and resolution of a different prompt. A sibling resolution can expose a previously omitted prompt.

An unknown host observation retains the last served rows. A permission-state agent with no named prompt IDs keeps its previous per-agent rows and makes the observation incomplete. When a publication is incomplete because one agent has more than 32 native prompt IDs, the retained input keeps previously known permission rows; a later complete native observation reconciles answered or removed prompts within the separate aggregate bound.
exclusions: Reading a permission-looking string from task or agent prose.
Fabricating an occurrence when a native identity is unknown.
Any additional permission poll, and any prompt argument or secret content.
An unlimited census or visibility guarantee beyond the per-agent and aggregate admission bounds.

statement: Each admitted native permission-prompt row has a stable occurrence identity derived from its actual agent and prompt IDs; incomplete observations and sibling resolution preserve that identity within the admitted bounded population, without guaranteeing visibility of every outstanding native prompt.
